evidence.content:
## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
2. The first execution counts as one of the three.
3. When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.

## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.

## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. Each execution attempt must time out after thirty seconds of execution.
2. An attempt that reaches the timeout must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An attempt starts at 12:00:00 and has not completed by 12:00:30. Orion records the attempt as failed at 12:00:30.

## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.

## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.

## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.

## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.

## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.

## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.

## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.

## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.

evidence.content:
## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job's initial execution fails, and so do its first and second retries. A third retry is performed. If that retry also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.

## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.

## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.

## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.

## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.

## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.

## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.

## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.

## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.

## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.

## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.

evidence.content:
## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
Job Q-31 fails on its initial execution and on three retries. Q-31 is not executed a fifth time.

## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31's initial execution fails at 08:14:10; the first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15. Each later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.

## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.

## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.

## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.

## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.

## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.

## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.

## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.

## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
Job Q-31 fails on its initial execution and on three retries. Q-31 is not executed a fifth time.

## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).

## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.

## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.

## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.

## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.

## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.

## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.

## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.

## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.

## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.

## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it. Renewal is driven by remaining lease life rather than a fixed cadence, and is rate-limited so that many workers cannot flood the lease service.

Normative rule
1. A worker must renew its lease when twenty seconds of lease life remain, provided work on the job is progressing.
2. A worker must never renew the same lease more often than once every fifteen seconds.
3. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 holds a ninety-second lease on Q-40 from 09:30:00. It renews at 09:31:10 (twenty seconds remaining); the lease now ends at 09:32:40, and W-2 may not renew again before 09:31:25.

## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
3. If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running; that execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows. A second cancellation for Q-40 arrives a minute later; Q-40 stays cancelled and nothing else about Q-40 changes.

## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 (key IK-1) is delivered at 11:00 and is active. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-1 at 11:02 is ignored. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-2 at 11:03 is rejected as conflicting.

## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.

## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.

Normative rule
1. When five dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within any rolling thirty-minute window, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The window is rolling: at each new dead-letter event Orion must count the events for that tenant in the preceding thirty minutes, including the new event.

Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:25, 08:31, 08:40 and 08:49. At 08:49 five events fall within the preceding thirty minutes, so an escalation is raised.

The promise is deliberately limited so that a slow job in one partition never stalls the others.

1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example

## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit history is kept for a bounded period so that investigations have a predictable window.

Normative rule
1. Audit history must remain queryable for one month, defined here as thirty calendar days from the moment each event is recorded.
2. Once an event is older than that window it may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June must remain queryable through 2 July and may be removed afterwards.

evidence.content:
## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.

## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker owns a delivered job for one and a half minutes unless the lease is renewed or released earlier.
2. When that ownership period ends without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00, never renews and never releases. At 09:31:30 ownership ends and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.

## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it. Renewal is driven by remaining lease life rather than a fixed cadence, and is rate-limited so that many workers cannot flood the lease service.

Normative rule
1. A worker must renew its lease when twenty seconds of lease life remain, provided work on the job is progressing.
2. A worker must never renew the same lease more often than once every fifteen seconds.
3. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 holds a ninety-second lease on Q-40 from 09:30:00. It renews at 09:31:10 (twenty seconds remaining); the lease now ends at 09:32:40, and W-2 may not renew again before 09:31:25.

## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
3. If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running; that execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows. A second cancellation for Q-40 arrives a minute later; Q-40 stays cancelled and nothing else about Q-40 changes.

## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 (key IK-1) is delivered at 11:00 and is active. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-1 at 11:02 is ignored. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-2 at 11:03 is rejected as conflicting.

## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.

## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding needs a human decision. Automatic dead-lettering hid genuine faults from tenants; Orion now keeps the job visible in a failed state until an operator has looked at it.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must leave the job in the failed state.
2. A job in the failed state must require operator review before any further action is taken on it.
3. Orion must not automatically move a job to the dead-letter queue.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20. Q-31 remains in the failed state and appears in the operator review list; nothing moves it to the dead-letter queue automatically.

## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. The threshold is tuned so that a brief burst does not page an operator while a sustained fault does.

Normative rule
1. When five dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within any rolling thirty-minute window, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The window is rolling: at each new dead-letter event Orion must count the events for that tenant in the preceding thirty minutes, including the new event.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:25, 08:31, 08:40 and 08:49. At 08:49 five events fall within the preceding thirty minutes, so an escalation is raised.

The promise is deliberately limited so that a slow job in one partition never stalls the others.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example

## Audit — how long records are kept

Normative rule
1. Audit history must remain queryable for one month, defined here as thirty calendar days from the moment each event is recorded.
2. Once an event is older than that window it may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June must remain queryable through 2 July and may be removed afterwards.

When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
After an execution attempt fails, the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt before every retry.
The retry wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen so repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it, which marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
A producer or operator may cancel a job.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue, where it can be inspected without blocking the queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

nodes.mission: Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
nodes.proposal_rationale: Synthesizes the common purpose of the supplied Orion job-processing rules. No existing Intent is shown.
The supplied claim identifies a worker as the executor of admitted jobs.
nodes.statement: Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.

nodes.proposal_rationale: Combines the supplied attempt definition, execution limit, inclusion of the first execution, and prohibition after the third unsuccessful execution.
nodes.statement: A job may have at most three execution attempts, including its first execution. One attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third execution ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claims specify a five-second retry wait that does not vary with attempt number.
nodes.statement: Before a retry after a failed attempt, wait five seconds. Do not shorten or lengthen this wait based on the attempt number.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim specifies a thirty-second execution-attempt timeout.
nodes.statement: Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires timed-out attempts to be recorded as failures and governed by the retry policy.
nodes.statement: Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

nodes.proposal_rationale: Combines the three-event escalation threshold with the specified one-hour window measured from the first event.
nodes.statement: Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim permits each delivery to carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
nodes.statement: Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.

nodes.proposal_rationale: Combines the key-retention duration and the stated treatment after that period.
nodes.statement: Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires an audit event for every job state transition.
nodes.statement: Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claims specify retention for thirty days after recording and permit deletion afterward.
nodes.statement: Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires automatic dead-letter routing after the final unsuccessful attempt.
nodes.statement: After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim makes explicit resubmission a necessary condition for executing a dead-lettered job again.
nodes.statement: A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires FIFO execution ordering among jobs within the same queue partition.
nodes.statement: Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claims explicitly exclude ordering guarantees between different queue partitions.
nodes.statement: Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The claim restricts ordering guarantees to those achievable without whole-service serialisation. This is a project-imposed boundary on how ordering may be realised.
nodes.statement: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.

nodes.proposal_rationale: Combines the requirement to ignore duplicate deliveries of an active job id with preservation of the active job's state.
nodes.statement: While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim permits cancellation by a producer or operator.
nodes.statement: Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires an already-running attempt to continue despite cancellation.
nodes.statement: Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim prohibits starting future attempts after cancellation.
nodes.statement: After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim defines the receiving worker's lease and its exclusion of a second worker.
nodes.statement: A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim specifies a sixty-second lease measured from delivery to the worker.
nodes.statement: The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim requires availability to other workers when a lease expires without renewal or release.
nodes.statement: When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

nodes.proposal_rationale: The supplied claim specifies the permitted renewal interval while work is progressing.
nodes.statement: While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.

nodes.proposal_rationale: Combines the requirement for a full-duration renewal from the renewal moment with the specified sixty-second lease duration.
nodes.statement: Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
2. The first execution counts as one of the three.
3. When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/L-audit-retention.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-L01"}],"known_addresses":[{"address_id":"ADDR-3a12d8a45c823c8c","subject":"Job execution attempts","facet":"Rules propositions.statement: Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker.
An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out.
A job must be executed at most three times in total.
The first execution counts as one of the three attempts.
When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Before every retry the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt.
The retry wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached, the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the timeout limit must be recorded as a failed attempt and the retry policy applies.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it, which marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
A producer or operator may cancel a job.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["ASSERT_CLAIM","CONFLICTS_WITH","SUPERSEDE","SUPPORTS_CLAIM"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
2. The first execution counts as one of the three.
3. When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K01"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L02","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T02/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Before a retry after a failed attempt, wait five seconds. Do not shorten or lengthen this wait based on the attempt number.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

A job may have at most three execution attempts, including its first execution. One attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third execution ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.
