{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job's initial execution fails, and so do its first and second retries. A third retry is performed. If that retry also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/L-audit-retention.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-L02"}],"known_addresses":[{"address_id":"ADDR-3a12d8a45c823c8c","subject":"Job execution attempts","facet":"Rules  Normative rule
-1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
-2. The first execution counts as one of the three.

 Example
-A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.

propositions.statement: Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker.
An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out.
Each job begins with one initial execution.
If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
The initial execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions and does not count as one of three total executions.
When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
An attempt that reaches the timeout is treated as failed, recorded as a failed attempt, and the retry policy applies.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored so the job is not executed twice because of redelivery.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it, which marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
A producer or operator may cancel a job.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["ASSERT_CLAIM","CONFLICTS_WITH","SUPERSEDE","SUPPORTS_CLAIM"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job's initial execution fails, and so do its first and second retries. A third retry is performed. If that retry also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I02"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J03","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T03/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Before a retry after a failed attempt, wait five seconds. Do not shorten or lengthen this wait based on the attempt number.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.

A job may have at most three execution attempts, including its first execution. One attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third execution ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
Job Q-31 fails on its initial execution and on three retries. Q-31 is not executed a fifth time.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31's initial execution fails at 08:14:10; the first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15. Each later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J03"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L04","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T04/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
Each job begins with one initial execution.
Executions per job are capped: if the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions.
When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
The initial execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt.
The retry wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute (thirty seconds).
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit must be recorded as a failed attempt and the retry rules take over.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored and the job is not run twice.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen so repeats can be recognised.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job as in hand and keeps other workers away from it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Before a retry after a failed attempt, wait five seconds. Do not shorten or lengthen this wait based on the attempt number.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. Each job begins with one initial execution.
2. If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
Job Q-31 fails on its initial execution and on three retries. Q-31 is not executed a fifth time.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example

","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

-Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear.
+Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.
 
 Normative rule
-1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
-2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

+3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure, or timeout.
Each job begins with one initial execution.
If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
The three retry executions are in addition to the job's initial execution.
When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds from the end of the failed execution.
The retry pause grows with each failure: before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry.
The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.
Every execution is subject to a time limit of half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit is a failed attempt and the retry rules apply.
While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery with the same job id must be ignored and the job is not run twice.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen so repeats can be recognised.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job in hand and keeps other workers away.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt, which runs to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three dead-letter events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

3. When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.

","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K04"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I05","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T05/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

 ## Execution — delay before a retry
 
-Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear.
+Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.
 
 Normative rule
-1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
-2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
+1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
+2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
+3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.
 
 Example
-Q-31's initial execution fails at 08:14:10; the first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15. Each later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Before a retry after a failed attempt, wait five seconds. Do not shorten or lengthen this wait based on the attempt number.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/L-audit-retention.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-L05"}],"known_addresses":[{"address_id":"ADDR-3a12d8a45c823c8c","subject":"Job execution attempts","facet":"Rules propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
A job has one original execution.
An original execution may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
The original execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.
Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds.
The wait before the first retry is measured from the end of the failed execution.
Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit must be recorded as a failed attempt and the retry rules apply.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job in hand and keeps other workers away.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt, which runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The three dead-letter events that raise an escalation must occur within one hour.
The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["ASSERT_CLAIM","CONFLICTS_WITH","SUPERSEDE","SUPPORTS_CLAIM"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K05"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I06","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T06/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule

that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence."},{"sentence_id":"EV-O-B06#S3","evidence_id":"EV-O-B06","text":"Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two twice."},{"sentence_id":"EV-O-D06#S3","evidence_id":"EV-O-D06","text":"While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be forgotten by Friday 14:00."},{"sentence_id":"EV-O-F06#S1","evidence_id":"EV-O-F06","text":"Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Before the first retry, the worker must wait 2 seconds. Before each later retry, the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry, capped at a maximum wait of 30 seconds.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.
