{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
Executions per job are capped: one original execution may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
A job has one original execution.
The original execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.
After a failed execution, the worker must wait two seconds before the first retry.
The wait before the first retry is measured from the end of the failed execution.
Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit must be recorded as a failed attempt and the retry rules apply.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job in hand and keeps other workers away from it.
A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The tenant dead-letter escalation window is one hour.
The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J06"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L07","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T07/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/L-audit-retention.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-L06"}],"known_addresses":[{"address_id":"ADDR-3a12d8a45c823c8c","subject":"Job execution attempts","facet":"Rules known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Before the first retry, the worker must wait 2 seconds. Before each later retry, the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry, capped at a maximum wait of 30 seconds.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
Measure the wait before the first retry from the end of the failed execution.
The worker lease must last 60 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 60-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

-Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.
+Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.
 
 Normative rule

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
A job has one original execution.
Executions per job are capped: one original execution may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
The original execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds.
The retry wait is measured from the end of the failed attempt.
The retry delay is a single fixed pause and must not be shortened or lengthened based on attempt number.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit is recorded as a failed attempt and retry rules apply.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job in hand and keeps other workers away.
A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Three dead-letter events for the same tenant raise an operator escalation.
The three dead-letter events must occur within one hour to raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running. That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J07"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L08","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T08/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/L-audit-retention.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-L07"}],"known_addresses":[{"address_id":"ADDR-3a12d8a45c823c8c","subject":"Job execution attempts","facet":"Rules known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Before the first retry, the worker must wait 2 seconds. Before each later retry, the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry, capped at a maximum wait of 30 seconds.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
Measure the wait before the first retry from the end of the failed execution.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 90-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
The worker lease must last 90 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-F09 grants a worker a lease on a delivered job and EV-O-G09 governs renewing that lease; both are dimensions of worker lease on a job.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-H09 governs cancelling a job, including effects on future and in-flight executions and repeated cancellation, which are dimensions of job cancellation.
drafts.subject: Job cancellation

drafts.rationale: EV-O-D09 governs ignoring further deliveries that carry an already active job id without changing that job's state.
drafts.subject: Duplicate delivery of an active job

drafts.rationale: EV-O-E09 governs retention and later forgetting of producer-chosen idempotency keys on deliveries.
drafts.subject: Job idempotency keys

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["BIND_TO_ADDRESS","CREATE_ADDRESS"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
3. If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
A job has one original execution.
The original execution may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
The original execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds after a failed execution.
The retry wait is measured from the end of the failed attempt.
The retry delay is a single fixed pause and must not be shortened or lengthened based on attempt number.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute.
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit is a failed attempt and the retry rules apply.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job grants the worker a lease that marks the job in hand and keeps other workers away.
A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to completion, failure or timeout.
A repeated cancellation of an already cancelled job is acknowledged; the job remains cancelled and its state is otherwise unchanged.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Three dead-letter events for the same tenant raise an operator escalation.
The tenant dead-letter events that raise an escalation must occur within one hour.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["ASSERT_CLAIM","CONFLICTS_WITH","SUPERSEDE","SUPPORTS_CLAIM"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
3. If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running; that execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows. A second cancellation for Q-40 arrives a minute later; Q-40 stays cancelled and nothing else about Q-40 changes.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E08"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K09","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T09/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Before the first retry, the worker must wait 2 seconds. Before each later retry, the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry, capped at a maximum wait of 30 seconds.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
Measure the wait before the first retry from the end of the failed execution.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 90-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
The worker lease must last 90 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule

2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

{"allowed_judgment_kinds":["ASSERT_CLAIM","CONFLICTS_WITH","SUPERSEDE","SUPPORTS_CLAIM"],"evidence":[{"evidence_id":"EV-O-A10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/A","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — attempt budget

Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution. One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution. Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.

Normative rule
1. One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions.
2. Once three retry executions have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

Example
Q-31 is executed once and then retried three times without success. Q-31 is not executed again.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/A-execution-attempts.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-A09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-C10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/C","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — time limit per execution

Workers can stall. To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/C-attempt-timeout.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-C09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-B10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/B","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. Operational review found that a growing pause made recovery times unpredictable for tenants; the delay is therefore a single fixed pause again.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10; its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15, and every later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/B-retry-delay.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-B09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-F10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/F","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — lease on a delivered job

Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease. The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it. Field experience shows that sixty seconds was too short for workers that perform a cold start before their first renewal.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent. At 09:31:30 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/F-worker-lease.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-F09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-G10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/G","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — keeping the lease alive

A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/G-lease-renewal.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-G09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-H10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/H","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Ownership — cancelling a job

Producers and operators can cancel jobs. Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way. Because producers retry their own requests, Orion may receive the same cancellation more than once; a repeated cancellation is simply acknowledged.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
3. If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

Example
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running; that execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows. A second cancellation for Q-40 arrives a minute later; Q-40 stays cancelled and nothing else about Q-40 changes.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/H-cancellation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-H09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-D10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/D","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 (key IK-1) is delivered at 11:00 and is active. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-1 at 11:02 is ignored. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-2 at 11:03 is rejected as conflicting.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/D-duplicate-delivery.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-D09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-E10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/E","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Input handling — idempotency-key memory

Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key. Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/E-idempotency-keys.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-E09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-K10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/K","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Delivery guarantees — ordering

Some producers rely on enqueue order. Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first. Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/K-ordering.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-K09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-I10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/I","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — after the last attempt

A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/I-final-failure.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-I09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-J10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/J","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
","artifact_ref":"orion/spec/J-operator-escalation.md","supersedes_evidence_id":"EV-O-J09"},{"evidence_id":"EV-O-L10","source_kind":"DOCUMENT","source_ref":"experiment://orion/T10/L","scope":["orion-jobs"],"content":"## Audit — how long records are kept

Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports. Audit events are kept for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

 ## Input handling — repeated deliveries
 
-A producer that times out may send the same job again. Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.
+A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.
 
 Normative rule
-1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
-2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
+1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
+2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.
 
 Example
-Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.

known_objects.text: Ordering guarantees must not depend on serialising the whole service.
Provide Orion job processing that follows the specified job lifecycle and operational rules.
Providing an ordering guarantee between jobs in different queue partitions is not a goal.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt already running; that attempt must continue to its own completion, failure, or timeout.
Before the first retry, the worker must wait 2 seconds. Before each later retry, the worker must wait twice as long as before the previous retry, capped at a maximum wait of 30 seconds.
Admitted jobs must be executed by a worker.
Guarantee first-in-first-out execution order among jobs in the same queue partition.
A worker receiving a job must hold a lease on it that marks the job as being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Retain an idempotency key for 24 hours from when it is first seen. After that period, the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
When an execution attempt reaches its time limit, stop that execution.
Support an optional idempotency key on each delivery, chosen by the producer.
Measure the wait before the first retry from the end of the failed execution.
Each renewal must extend the lease for the full 90-second lease duration measured from the moment of renewal.
Retain each audit event for 30 days after recording it. After that period, the event may be deleted.
Record an attempt that reaches its timeout as a failed attempt and apply the retry policy.

Each job begins with one initial execution. If the initial execution is unsuccessful, at most three retry executions are permitted in addition to it. One execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that succeeds, fails, or times out. When the third retry ends without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Record every state transition of a job as an audit event.
Raise operator escalation when three dead-letter events for the same tenant occur within a one-hour window measured from the first of those three events.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
While a job with a given job id is active, ignore any further delivery carrying the same job id without changing the active job's state.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
While work is progressing, permit lease renewal every 30 seconds.
Allow a producer or operator to cancel a job.
The worker lease must last 90 seconds from delivery of the job to the worker.
Each execution attempt must have a timeout of 30 seconds.

drafts.subject: Duplicate delivery of an active job
